name: performing-artist-agi-boundary
computation: Single filer, born 1998-11-20. W-2 Example Theater box 1 $9,000.00 (box 2 $300.00) with box 12 code L $300.00, W-2 Example Opera box 1 $6,500.00 (box 2 $200.00), and a 1099-INT of $500.00. AGI before Schedule 1 line 12 = 9,000 + 6,500 + 500 = $16,000.00, exactly the section 62(b)(1)(C) limit ('does not exceed $16,000' passes). Form 2106, Stage actor, capacity PerformingArtist, employers both W-2s: travel $600.00, other $1,400.00 (agent fees, voice lessons), meals $200.00, no reimbursements, no vehicles. Line 6 column A = 0 + 0 + 600 + 1,400 = $2,000.00; column B = $200.00. Line 7 = code L $300.00 + $0.00 = $300.00. Reimbursement Allocation Worksheet ratio = 200 / 2,200 = 0.0909 = 0.091 to three decimals; 7B = 300 x 0.091 = $27.30; 7A = $272.70. Line 8A = 2,000.00 - 272.70 = $1,727.30; 8B = 200.00 - 27.30 = $172.70. Line 9 column A = $1,727.30; column B = 50% x 172.70 = $86.35. Line 10 = 1,727.30 + 86.35 = $1,813.65, rounded to $1,814 on Schedule 1 line 12. Tests: two employers each paying $200 or more (9,000 and 6,500); expenses $1,813.65 exceed 10% x $15,500 = $1,550; AGI $16,000 is at most $16,000; unmarried. Form 1040 line 1a = $15,500.00; line 2b = $500.00; line 9 = $16,000.00; line 11a/11b = 16,000 - 1,814 = $14,186.00; line 12e = $16,100.00, so line 15 = $0.00 and line 16 tax = $0.00 (the 2026 draft Tax Table would read 1,453 for a taxable income of 14,186, which is below the standard deduction). Line 25a = $300.00 + $200.00 = $500.00.
